title: Twin-Turbo Fireball 320
subtitle: 1939 Buick Business Coupe
summary: 700 HP E85 straight-eight engine packaging solution wrapped in a stretched 1939 Buick Business Coupe touring supercar chassis.
narrative: A high-horsepower forced induction packaging study built around Buick's iconic 320 cubic inch Fireball straight-eight powerplant.
Engineered for E85 output targeting 700 HP and housed within a custom-stretched 1939 Buick Business Coupe body.
Note: The accompanying gallery view features an AI-generated visual representation of the proposed straight-eight engine build.

title: Project VôôDôô Chīle
subtitle: 1948 Studebaker Champion 4-Door Deluxe Grand Touring Restomod
summary: A 1948 Studebaker Champion 4-door Deluxe Grand Touring restomod concept featuring Papa Legba veve pinstriping, pure silver rounds embedded in the dash, and custom grand touring architecture.

specifications.detailing: Papa Legba veve pinstriping & embedded pure silver dash rounds

narrative: Project VôôDôô Chīle takes the distinctive post-war silhouette of a 1948 Studebaker Champion 4-door Deluxe and reimagines it as a long-legged Grand Touring cruiser.
The aesthetic blends subtle occult-inspired custom detailing—including Papa Legba veve pinstriping and pure silver rounds embedded directly into the dash—with clean restomod proportions.
While the real Studebaker currently languishes in storage waiting for clear shop bandwidth, the design and treatment studies are fully mapped out for when fabrication finally kicks off.

title: Trips
subtitle: 1959 Pontiac Catalina Safari, Custom Cruiser
summary: A 1959 Pontiac Catalina Safari wagon built as a custom cruiser: a 461-cubic-inch Pontiac stroker purring out 500 hp under an updated Tri-Power, a ZF 8-speed behind it, meant for that road trip and not to be stopped by the Rockies.

specifications.output: ~500 hp / ~575 lb-ft, built to purr: aluminum D-port heads, mild hydraulic roller cam, pump gas
specifications.induction: Updated Tri-Power: FiTech 3x2 throttle-body EFI controlling the go juice
specifications.transmission: ZF 8HP90 8-speed automatic (Dodge), BOP adapter kit, standalone controller
specifications.suspension: Air suspension, double A-arm front, triangulated 4-link rear
specifications.brakes: Big brakes behind big wheels: not a racer, but a surprise in a corner
specifications.finish: Bronze metallic, gold wheels, tan interior
specifications.interior: Full creature comforts: entertainment, climate control, heated/cooled seats; rear-facing third row, folds flat for luggage; no cupholders
specifications.purpose: Custom cruiser for road trips and not intimidated by the Sepulveda Pass or the Rockies.
specifications.status: Dream: car in hand, waiting its turn to enter the Projects pipeline

narrative: Trips is three of a kind, and this wagon is counted in threes. In Three Card Brag, a prial of three is trips and a prial of treys is the winning hand; on the road, trips are the journeys this wagon exists to take. The emblem is a small fan of three treys, spades, clubs and hearts, and each card takes a count. The spade leads for the Tri-Power and its three throttle bodies: the power, at the front of the car and the front of the fan. The club stands in for the three rows of seats: club seating is the old railroad term for lounge seating in a car built to carry a crowd in comfort. The heart closes the fan with the people in the seats, community and good will, the cargo that matters. A spade and a heart are near inversions, one shape flipped and its color swapped, and the fan runs from power at the start to people at the end. The three card fan logo belongs on the car; the wordmark in the Alfa Slab One font is the lettering reserved for text about the car.

The mission calibrates everything: a custom cruiser, not a drag car and not a show car, built to take steep grades in an easy lope while weighing in at around 5,000 pounds. The engine is the Pontiac block of the Tri-Power GTOs, a 389 stroked to 461 cubic inches, and the target is 500 horsepower that purrs. Displacement and head flow do the work so the cam stays mild, idling smooth and pulling from just off idle. The updated Tri-Power is FiTech throttle-body EFI on the three-deuce intake for fuel management. Behind it sits a ZF 8HP90 eight-speed automatic on a catalog BOP adapter kit, chosen because more gears mean a smoother ride and a cruise rpm that barely wakes the engine. The chassis stiffening is hidden; there is no visible cage.

The car in the yard becomes the car in the render: bronze metallic over a tan interior, gold wheels, a full refinish. Trips is not a patina car. The cabin is full creature comfort: entertainment, climate control, heated and cooled seats on the spec sheet, three rows with the third row facing rearward, folding flat when the trip needs luggage instead of people. One cupholder rule stands: there are none. Big wheels carry big brakes, and the suspension brief lets the wagon surprise someone in a corner without ever pretending to be a racer.
For now the Safari waits its turn in the yard. The constraint is bandwidth, not intent: when a slot opens in the Projects pipeline, Trips promotes from Dream to Project and the build begins.

The 1959 Safari waiting its turn in the yard.

title: The Surrey
subtitle: Open-Air Surrey on a 1950s Chevy 1-Ton Frame
summary: A Hawaii-style open surrey built on a borrowed-then-gifted Chevy 1-ton frame: a hunted '40s/'50s nose, rows of weatherproof benches under a fringed top, and a rear-facing last row - built to carry the neighborhood around the beach at leisure.

specifications.chassis: Chevrolet 1-ton pickup ladder frame (1950s, 3800 class), Dana 60 rear axle - in hand
specifications.front: Donor wanted: 1940s/50s car or truck front Sheetmetal - windshield frame, firewall, door posts, front clip (free is best, cheap is neccessary; unsalvageable from the A-pillars back preferred)
specifications.rearBody: Open platform, reproduction rear fenders if I can't find a free set to use.
specifications.seating: Driver's row + 3-4 weatherproof benches + rear-facing final row
specifications.engine: TBD - small diesel brief: torque first, quiet, no clatter
specifications.performance: ~35 mph cruising, 50 mph max briefly; sand and waterline capable
specifications.status: Frame in hand / donor front section hunted

narrative: The Surrey is an open-air people-carrier in the Hawaii mold: a steel floor for the drivers row, a wood platform for the passengers, a fringed surrey top, and rows of seats, built on the simplest platform in the fleet - a 1950s Chevrolet 1-ton ladder frame. Ahead of the platform, a donor front section supplies the windshield frame, firewall, door posts, and front clip; everything behind that is open air, weatherproof benches, and a final row facing backward so kids of all ages can dangle their feet off the back.

The frame was never supposed to stay. It was borrowed so Project Not for Higher could sit on a rolling chassis for its tare-weight run: the frame arrived without wheels, a set of tires and wheels turned up at a great price. When the frame return was offered, the lender said keep it. A big ladder frame with a Dana 60 rear and good rubber is not something I can let go - and a platform this simple can carry anything, which is the whole Surrey philosophy.

Power is undecided, and the brief is a personality, not a part number: torque is the keyword, something neat and small, which to me says diesel, but who knows what I'll find. Thirty-five miles an hour might be the common 'fast' speed, slower cruising would be more common.  And fifty could be a brief maximum with passengers aboard if there were a need to get somewhere. The capability that actually matters is at the end of the road - off the pavement, onto the sand, and down to the water.

The Surrey is a social vehicle. There's an unofficial charitable crew that meets at a house down the street from me whose premise is beer, barbecue, and silly games: This is the composition I imagine for my intended passengers, and, hey, maybe the Elks at the pier and whoever else can use a slow ride.  I emphasize here that this is not business venture, just a neat personal vehicle.

gallery.caption: The Surrey as envisioned, fringed top and all.
Here we are loading up the borrowed frame wearing the cheap shoes.
